clinician.trajectory_summary: A healthy 3-year-old girl presented with a 5-day history of right-sided cheek and eye swelling and pain, associated with right-sided green nasal discharge. Initial examination revealed diffuse erythematous swelling around the right cheek, jawline, and eye. She was initially suspected to have periorbital cellulitis and treated with oral antibiotics, which proved ineffective. Cranial imaging performed at approximately 3 weeks of symptom onset demonstrated a large central but predominantly right-sided nasopharyngeal tumor extending into the ethmoid sinuses, orbits (with medial recti distortion), infratemporal fossa, pterygoid muscles, and anterior and middle cranial fossae with skull base destruction. MRI confirmed the tumor filling the posterior nasal passages and nasopharynx, eroding the anterior clivus border, extending into the anterior right middle cranial fossa with extension into the right orbit distorting the medial rectus muscle. Staging and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-metastatic parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma. Chemoradiotherapy was subsequently initiated.
